title: Two pointers
summary: Put one pointer at each end of a sorted list and move the one that brings you closer to the goal.
idea: On sorted data, each comparison tells you which end can never be part of the answer, so one pointer moves inward every step.

signals.see: The input is sorted, or sorting it would not lose anything you need.
signals.think: Start a pointer at each end. Sorted order tells you which side to move.

signals.see: You need a pair or triple with a target sum.
signals.think: Too small? Move the left pointer right. Too big? Move the right pointer left. For triples, fix one item and run two pointers on the rest.

signals.see: You must compare items from both ends, like a palindrome check.
signals.think: Walk inward from both ends and stop where they meet.

signals.see: You must do it in place with O(1) extra space.
signals.think: Use a read pointer and a write pointer moving the same way.

phrasings: Prices are listed from cheapest to most expensive. Find two different items that cost exactly your budget.
Check whether a product code reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring dashes.
Count the pairs of runners whose combined lap time is under a limit, given sorted times.

picture.title: Squeeze from both ends
picture.alt: On the left, every pair of items is tried, costing n times n checks. On the right, a pointer at each end of a sorted list compares the sum with the target and moves one pointer inward, so the list is crossed once.
picture.caption: Each step rules out a whole row of pairs, because the list is sorted.

after.label: Pattern: lo and hi move inward

code.py:
def pair_in_sorted(nums, target):
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums) - 1  #@init
    while lo < hi:  #@loop
        total = nums[lo] + nums[hi]  #@sum
        if total == target: return [lo, hi]  #@found
        if total < target: lo += 1  #@left
        else: hi -= 1  #@right
    return []  #@none

visualiser.inputHelp: Up to 12 whole numbers between -99 and 99, smallest first, separated by commas. The target is one whole number.

template.js:
function solve(items, target) {
  let lo = 0 // one pointer at each end of SORTED items
  let hi = items.length - 1
  while (lo < hi) { // stop when the pointers meet
    const total = items[lo] + items[hi]
    if (total === target) return [lo, hi] // found it
    if (total < target) lo++ // need a bigger sum: only moving lo right can help
    else hi-- // need a smaller sum: only moving hi left can help
  }
  return [] // pointers met: no pair
}

oneLiner: lo, hi = 0, n−1; while lo < hi: too small → lo++, too big → hi−−

exercise.prompt: times is sorted from smallest to largest. Count the pairs of different positions i < j whose times add up to strictly less than limit. When times[lo] + times[hi] is under the limit, every item from lo + 1 to hi pairs with lo. Fill in the missing count.
hints: If times[lo] + times[hi] is under the limit, swapping hi for any smaller item keeps it under. That is hi − lo pairs at once.
Add hi − lo to count, then move lo right. Otherwise move hi left.

complexity.why: Every step moves one pointer inward, so there are at most n − 1 steps. Only two indexes are stored. If you must sort first, time becomes O(n log n).

mistakes: Using two pointers on unsorted data. Sort first, or use a hash map instead.
Looping while lo <= hi, which pairs an item with itself.
Moving the wrong pointer: a sum that is too small needs lo to move right, not hi.
Forgetting to skip equal values when the answer must list distinct pairs or triples.
Sorting when the question needs the original positions. Keep the index with each value.

quiz.question: In a sorted list, the sum at lo and hi is too small. Which move is right?
quiz.explain: Only a bigger left item can raise the sum. Moving hi left could only make it smaller.

quiz.question: Why does the loop run while lo < hi rather than lo <= hi?
choices: So an item is never paired with itself
Because hi starts past the end
quiz.explain: When lo equals hi both pointers sit on the same item, and a pair needs two different positions.

quiz.question: The list is not sorted and you need the original positions of a pair. What is the simplest O(n) choice?
choices: A hash map of value to index
quiz.explain: Sorting costs O(n log n) and moves the positions. A one-pass hash map finds the pair in O(n) and keeps the indexes.

interviewTip: Say why moving a pointer is safe: “if the sum is too small, lo cannot pair with anything left of hi, so drop it”. That one sentence proves the method is correct.
